harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: LDAP directory is operational on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test. The staged LDIF was imported unchanged, node2 finds both users, writes require the authenticated administrator, and all functionality persisted through sequential node restarts.
actions_performed: Installed CentOS 5-compatible OpenLDAP packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured and boot-enabled slapd on node1 with administrator-only write access.
Generated and stored the administrator credential root-only on node1.
Allowed LDAP access from node2 through the persistent firewall configuration.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Directory contains the supplied identities and mail addresses unchanged
evidence.summary: Database and LDAP queries show alex/alex@branch.test and sam/sam@branch.test.

evidence.requirement: Node2 can search the people subtree and find both users
evidence.summary: Node2 successfully returned both inetOrgPerson entries before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Updates require an authenticated administrator and anonymous writes fail
evidence.summary: Post-restart anonymous modification failed with authentication required; an authenticated administrator modification succeeded, was verified, and was reverted.

evidence.requirement: Legacy OS release and kernel preserved

evidence.summary: Boot ID changed from c4d6cac8-54e6-4410-8000-000000000000 to 9d19abb5-6e19-43f0-8000-000000000000; slapd, TCP/389, firewall state, directory data, and remote searches recovered.
Boot ID changed from f4637d3e-ec45-4732-8000-000000000000 to 78dc4411-cfc5-4fea-8000-000000000000; the LDAP client and successful remote people search recovered.
